title: e2e Testing with Cypress
summary: Why we test, the three kinds of tests (unit, integration, end-to-end), and how to set up Cypress in a Vite + React app: install it, point cypress.config.js at the dev server, write specs in cypress/e2e/, and run them in the Cypress window or headless. The second lesson writes assertions for each feature of the Pokémon app. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Install Cypress in a React app and write an end-to-end test that checks a page renders and a feature works.

steps.title: Read both lessons
steps.detail: Read 'Cypress and React' and 'Cypress Assertions', especially 'Unit vs Integration vs e2e'.
steps.doneWhen: You can give one example of each test type.

steps.title: Sort your Myflix tests by type
steps.detail: Myflix already has Vitest + Testing Library tests in assignments/week-02/netflix/src/test. Run them and label each file unit or integration. Cypress adds the third kind: a real browser clicking through the app.
steps.doneWhen: All tests pass and you've labeled each test file.

steps.title: Set up Cypress in a scratch app
steps.detail: In a throwaway Vite app: npm install cypress --save-dev, add a cypress.config.js with baseUrl http://localhost:5173/ (from the lesson), and create cypress/e2e/home.cy.js. Start npm run dev, then npx cypress open.
steps.doneWhen: The Cypress window lists home.cy.js and the test turns green.

steps.title: List Myflix e2e scenarios
steps.detail: Write three user journeys you'd test end to end in Myflix (for example: add a title to My List, rate it, reload and see it still there). Don't add Cypress to Myflix unless an assignment asks.
steps.doneWhen: You have three scenarios written as 'user does X, sees Y'.

concepts.meaning: Checks one small function or piece on its own.
Checks that a few pieces work together, like a component and its hook.
Drives the real app in a browser the way a user would.
The check in a test, like .should("have.length", 1).
Running tests without opening a visible browser window, as CI does.
